item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J03510","case1_error":"Gives unsupported $12,000 after the correct formula, which yields $23,248.","case2_error":"Counts five family members instead of four, using the wrong divisor for equal shares.","reason":"The first supplies an incorrect final number after a correct formula; the second constructs an incorrect headcount.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03511","case1_error":"Omits Ted's four eaten cookies from the remaining-cookie calculation.","case2_error":"Reports Tully's current age rather than his age one year ago.","reason":"The first omits a stated consumption from the requested balance; the second correctly calculates and reports the wrong temporal quantity.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03512","case1_error":"Charges for only one of two sandwiches and evaluates the displayed sum as $30.25 instead of $32.25.","case2_error":"Sets feeding cost equal to purchase cost, ignoring the stated 20% increase.","reason":"The first omits an item multiplicity and miscalculates its sum; the second replaces a percentage-increase relation with equality.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03513","case1_error":"Evaluates 18 months plus six years as 8.5 years instead of 7.5.","case2_error":"Equates one-sixth of a day with 24 hours, ignoring the fractional duration.","reason":"The first incorrectly evaluates a correctly specified duration sum; the second writes an incorrect conversion relation that drops the fraction.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J03514","case1_error":"Treats ten ads per company as ten ads overall, omitting the three-company multiplier.","case2_error":"Treats monthly material costs as per-vehicle costs, multiplying those costs by production counts.","reason":"The first fails to aggregate a per-company quantity; the second repeatedly charges an already aggregate cost as a unit cost.","judgment":"different"}]}
